main_text.p: pinquis parcerent, nec liberi à paren-tibus manus abstinerent, nec fana & aræ supplicibus ad misericordiam prodesent, civitatem fortuna & viribus exhausit, atque ita calamitatibus omnis generis obruit, ut quocunque te verteres, miserrima rerum facies conspiceretur. Tanta acerbitas partium-tum fuit: locum proverbio res dedit ut quævis cruenta & atrox seditio Corcyræa diceretur. Finem accepit immanis tragœdia decurrente æstate anni vii belli Peloponnesiaci, qui concurrebat cum Olympiadis lxxxviii anno quarto. Nec Corcyræis solum calamitati hæc tragœdia fuit, sed exemplo quoque plurimis Græciæ civitatibus no-suit, quæ eodem furoris æstu correptæ in similimos motus civiles cruentos exarsere. Historia fusè à Thucydide descripta est libro iii. Victoria penes populares ope Atheniensium adjutos stetit, à quibus crimini adversæ factioni datum, quòd popularem statum subruere satagerent. A quo tempore penes populum summa reipublicæ potestas Corcyræ[?] mansit, perstititque civitas in societate Atheniensium, quietè usa domi per annos quasi lii, ad annum sci-licet tertium Olympiadis ci. Eo autem anno[?] vicinorum Zacynthiorum exem-plo

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse side: red and black marks and fragments along the left edge and lower left (e.g. "Syc 3ʀ", "Zac 3ʀS") are not printed here and are left out. The first letter of the line "Corcyræ" is faded and partly covered by a red mark; the reading is doubtful. The word before "vicinorum" is faded; "anno" is a likely reading. The line "partium" ends in a dash that may be a printed hyphen or a dash. The catchword "plo" lies below the last full line, so the final line ends with the hyphenated "exem-".
